raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Tool names are user input and must be kept private. 

Previously, WARN logs for malformed tool calls did include tool names, e.g.:
```
Tool call 'my_tool' has arguments that are not valid JSON (420 chars); coercing to an empty object so the conversation can continue.
```

After this change, the WARN log does no longer print sensitive information:
```
Tool call has arguments that are not valid JSON (420 chars); coercing to an empty object so the conversation can continue.
```

Upside: vllm can be used in privacy-relevant applications without custom patches
Downside: debugging is more complex in case of malformed tool calls. We could add DEBUG logs that include the tool name, if strongly desired.

files.patch:
@@ -720,10 +720,9 @@ def _postprocess_messages(messages: list[ConversationMessage]) -> None:
                                 # leave the conversation unrecoverable. Coerce
                                 # to an empty object so the turn can proceed.
                                 logger.warning(
-                                    "Tool call %r has arguments that are not valid "
+                                    "Tool call has arguments that are not valid "
                                     "JSON (%d chars); coercing to an empty object "
                                     "so the conversation can continue.",
-                                    function.get("name"),
                                     len(content),
                                 )
                                 parsed = None
@@ -736,9 +735,8 @@ def _postprocess_messages(messages: list[ConversationMessage]) -> None:
                                 # "42", "true").
                                 # Chat templates require a mapping.
                                 logger.warning(
-                                    "Tool call %r arguments decoded to %s, not a "
+                                    "Tool call arguments decoded to %s, not a "
                                     "JSON object; coercing to an empty object.",
-                                    function.get("name"),
                                     type(parsed).__name__,
                                 )
                             parsed = {}
